# Report usage across every tool round, not just the last

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#93
Labels: priority:medium, type:feature, size:S, area:api

## Why

`afterModelResponse` is the hook a deployer reaches for when they need to record what a turn cost — an audit entry, a billing line, a usage budget. It is called once per user message, after the round loop exits, and is handed the `lastUsage` local: `chatOrchestrator.ts` assigns `lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage` on each round, so what the hook receives is the usage of the final provider call alone.

For a turn that answered directly, that is the whole turn. For a turn that called tools, it is the last leg of several, and the earlier rounds — including the one carrying the customer's question and the full tool results — are not counted anywhere. A deployer billing or budgeting from this hook under-counts exactly the expensive turns, and nothing in the signature hints at it. The current behaviour is recorded in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` so it is at least discoverable, but documenting a surprising number is weaker than not producing one.

Raised by the reviewer on HALEngine#83, which recorded the behaviour but could not change it: that PR's ticket scoped itself to specifying the seam, not altering the orchestrator.

## What to do

Decide, and make the signature say the answer. Two shapes are worth weighing, and the issue should record why the other was rejected:

- Accumulate across rounds and pass the sum, keeping one `usage` argument. Simple for the common case, and it silently changes what an existing consumer records — the number gets larger for tool-heavy turns, which is the point, but it is a behaviour change worth a MINOR bump and a changelog line that says so.
- Pass both, for example the summed total plus the per-round breakdown, so a consumer that wants provider-call granularity keeps it. More faithful, wider surface.

Whichever is chosen, a turn that ran no tools must report exactly what it reports today, so the common path does not move.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A turn driven through two tool rounds reports usage covering every provider call in that turn, asserted against a scripted provider whose rounds report known, different token counts
- [ ] A turn with no tool calls reports exactly what it reports today, pinned by the existing test remaining unedited
- [ ] A provider that reports no usage on some rounds does not make the total `undefined` or `NaN`: the rounds that reported are still counted, and a turn where nothing reported still reports nothing
- [ ] The type of what the hook receives makes the answer unambiguous, so a reader does not have to open the orchestrator to learn whether it is a sum
- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded under-counting line with the new behaviour, and the CHANGELOG entry states the change in what an existing consumer will record
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass, with no `any` in the public API

## Tech notes

Out of scope: the audit entry or billing record itself, which is a consumer's concern; token accounting for anything other than the provider calls the orchestrator makes; and the `stop` chunk's own `usage` shape, which providers already populate and this issue only aggregates.

Key files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `lastUsage` local and the `afterModelResponse` call site), `src/types/ai.ts` (`UsageMetadata`), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.

17	- [ ] **counts the rounds that reported usage when one round reports none, and reports nothing when no round did** — rounds reporting 7/2/9, nothing, and 5/1/6 sum to 12/3/15 (today: 5/1/6), and a turn in which no round reported still hands the hook `undefined`, never `NaN`
18	  `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.acceptance.test.ts`
19	
20	Existing tests that must stay green and unedited: `receives collected response text and usage` (the no-tool path, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L236`) and `keeps the usage an earlier round reported when a later round reports none` (`#L527`, a one-reporting-round sum equals that round).
21	
22	## Facets
23	
24	- [ ] Accumulate `outcome.usage` across rounds in `chatOrchestrator.ts` instead of overwriting `lastUsage`: a round with no usage adds nothing, and a turn with no reported usage stays `undefined`; the first acceptance test goes green
25	- [ ] Skipping an unreported round keeps the total a number; the second acceptance test goes green
26	- [ ] Make the signature say it is a sum: name or document the `afterModelResponse` usage parameter in `OrchestratorHooks` (`src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts`) and, if a breakdown is passed too, type it, with no `any`; regenerate the CLAUDE.md hooks block if it is generated from the declaration
27	- [ ] Record in the issue which of the two shapes was chosen and why the other was rejected
28	- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` → `Changed`: state that an existing `afterModelResponse` consumer now records a larger number on tool-heavy turns, and that a no-tool turn is unchanged (MINOR bump per the ticket)
29	- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`: the under-counting line is already replaced by the "Usage reported to afterModelResponse" section on this branch; re-run `node scripts/check-spec-anchor-names.mjs --fix specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` after any edit that shifts the cited tests
30	- [ ] `example/full-config.ts` already comments that `usage` is "the turn's total over every tool round"; after this change that comment becomes true, so leave it or tighten it, but do not let CHANGELOG and example disagree
31	
32	## Out of scope
33	
34	- The audit entry or billing record itself: a consumer's concern
35	- Token accounting for anything other than the provider calls the orchestrator makes (no `generateStructured`, no prompt-building cost)
36	- The `stop` chunk's own `usage` shape, which providers already populate
37	- The `error instanceof Error` gate on `onError`, still recorded under "Measured semantics — out of scope" in the spec

> For a turn that answered directly, that is the whole turn. For a turn that called tools, it is the last leg of several, and the earlier rounds — including the one carrying the customer's question and the full tool results — are not counted anywhere. **Strategy: `direct`** — the seam exists today: `createChatOrchestrator` takes a real `AIProvider` and `OrchestratorHooks`, so a scripted provider whose rounds carry known, different `usage` values drives the tool loop end to end and the `afterModelResponse` hook observes what the turn reported. The tests assert on the hook's third argument (`usage`) and are indifferent to which of the ticket's two shapes is chosen: the acceptance criterion that the no-tool test `receives collected response text and usage` stays unedited means the third argument on a single-round turn must deep-equal the provider's `UsageMetadata`, so the sum has to arrive in that argument either way. A per-round breakdown, if the implementer chooses to pass one, is additional surface these tests neither require nor forbid.

This repository's `tests.list` descriptor carries only `id`, `name` and `file` (see `scripts/lore-list-tests.mjs`), so there is no in-test spec anchor to stamp; traceability is the trailing `[validated by: <title>](...#Lnn)` citation in the spec, per AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links.

## Done when these pass

- [ ] **reports the sum of three provider calls when a turn runs two tool rounds** — rounds reporting 100/10/110, 200/20/220 and 300/30/330 tokens are handed to the hook as 600/60/660; today it receives 300/30/330
  `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.acceptance.test.ts`
- [ ] **counts the rounds that reported usage when one round reports none, and reports nothing when no round did** — rounds reporting 7/2/9, nothing, and 5/1/6 sum to 12/3/15 (today: 5/1/6), and a turn in which no round reported still hands the hook `undefined`, never `NaN`
  `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.acceptance.test.ts`

Existing tests that must stay green and unedited: `receives collected response text and usage` (the no-tool path, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L236`) and `keeps the usage an earlier round reported when a later round reports none` (`#L527`, a one-reporting-round sum equals that round).

## Facets

- [ ] Accumulate `outcome.usage` across rounds in `chatOrchestrator.ts` instead of overwriting `lastUsage`: a round with no usage adds nothing, and a turn with no reported usage stays `undefined`; the first acceptance test goes green

- [ ] `example/full-config.ts` already comments that `usage` is "the turn's total over every tool round"; after this change that comment becomes true, so leave it or tighten it, but do not let CHANGELOG and example disagree

## Out of scope

- The audit entry or billing record itself: a consumer's concern
- Token accounting for anything other than the provider calls the orchestrator makes (no `generateStructured`, no prompt-building cost)

# Definition of Done

> `chatOrchestrator.ts` assigns `lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage` on each round, so what the hook receives is the usage of the final provider call alone.
>
> For a turn that answered directly, that is the whole turn. For a turn that called tools, it is the last leg of several, and the earlier rounds — including the one carrying the customer's question and the full tool results — are not counted anywhere. A deployer billing or budgeting from this hook under-counts exactly the expensive turns, and nothing in the signature hints at it.

**Strategy: `direct`** — the seam exists today: `createChatOrchestrator` takes a real `AIProvider` and `OrchestratorHooks`, so a scripted provider whose rounds carry known, different `usage` values drives the tool loop end to end and the `afterModelResponse` hook observes what the turn reported. No double is needed.

The tests assert on the hook's third argument (`usage`) and are indifferent to which of the ticket's two shapes is chosen: the acceptance criterion that the no-tool test `receives collected response text and usage` stays unedited means the third argument on a single-round turn must deep-equal the provider's `UsageMetadata`, so the sum has to arrive in that argument either way. A per-round breakdown, if the implementer chooses to pass one, is additional surface these tests neither require nor forbid.

This repository's `tests.list` descriptor carries only `id`, `name` and `file` (see `scripts/lore-list-tests.mjs`), so there is no in-test spec anchor to stamp; traceability is the trailing `[validated by: <title>](...#Lnn)` citation in the spec, per AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links.

## Done when these pass

- [ ] **reports the sum of three provider calls when a turn runs two tool rounds** — rounds reporting 100/10/110, 200/20/220 and 300/30/330 tokens are handed to the hook as 600/60/660; today it receives 300/30/330
  `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.acceptance.test.ts`
- [ ] **counts the rounds that reported usage when one round reports none, and reports nothing when no round did** — rounds reporting 7/2/9, nothing, and 5/1/6 sum to 12/3/15 (today: 5/1/6), and a turn in which no round reported still hands the hook `undefined`, never `NaN`
  `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.acceptance.test.ts`

Existing tests that must stay green and unedited: `receives collected response text and usage` (the no-tool path, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L236`) and `keeps the usage an earlier round reported when a later round reports none` (`#L527`, a one-reporting-round sum equals that round).

## Facets

- [ ] Accumulate `outcome.usage` across rounds in `chatOrchestrator.ts` instead of overwriting `lastUsage`: a round with no usage adds nothing, and a turn with no reported usage stays `undefined`; the first acceptance test goes green
- [ ] Skipping an unreported round keeps the total a number; the second acceptance test goes green
- [ ] Make the signature say it is a sum: name or document the `afterModelResponse` usage parameter in `OrchestratorHooks` (`src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts`) and, if a breakdown is passed too, type it, with no `any`; regenerate the CLAUDE.md hooks block if it is generated from the declaration
- [ ] Record in the issue which of the two shapes was chosen and why the other was rejected
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` → `Changed`: state that an existing `afterModelResponse` consumer now records a larger number on tool-heavy turns, and that a no-tool turn is unchanged (MINOR bump per the ticket)
- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`: the under-counting line is already replaced by the "Usage reported to afterModelResponse" section on this branch; re-run `node scripts/check-spec-anchor-names.mjs --fix specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` after any edit that shifts the cited tests
- [ ] `example/full-config.ts` already comments that `usage` is "the turn's total over every tool round"; after this change that comment becomes true, so leave it or tighten it, but do not let CHANGELOG and example disagree

## Out of scope

- The audit entry or billing record itself: a consumer's concern
- Token accounting for anything other than the provider calls the orchestrator makes (no `generateStructured`, no prompt-building cost)
- The `stop` chunk's own `usage` shape, which providers already populate
- The `error instanceof Error` gate on `onError`, still recorded under "Measured semantics — out of scope" in the spec
